x: Gibberellin is keyed: it drives cell and stem elongation, as in bolting and dwarf plants growing tall. Auxin also elongates cells, but it is linked mainly to tropisms and apical dominance.
ABA stands for abscisic acid, the plant stress hormone that closes stomata and keeps buds and seeds dormant.
ABA is the stress hormone: it builds up in drought and closes stomata to save water. Auxin, gibberellin and cytokinin promote growth.
t: Discriminate growth promoters from the growth inhibitor.

x: Option C is incorrect: ABA inhibits growth and promotes dormancy. Auxin, gibberellin and cytokinin all promote growth.
t: Discriminate growth promoters from the growth inhibitor.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: tropisms come from auxin moving to one side of a shoot; rooting is a separate effect.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a parallel effect.

x: Both are true and R explains A: gibberellin triggers enzymes that start germination, which is how it breaks seed dormancy.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: ABA closes stomata, cutting water loss through transpiration.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: cytokinin regulates growth by promoting cell division and keeps leaves green longer by delaying senescence.
Statement A is true: auxin promotes rooting, as in rooting powders. Statement B is false because germination effects belong to gibberellin.
t: Discriminate auxin effects from gibberellin effects.

x: Auxin causes apical dominance, gibberellin stem elongation, cytokinin delays senescence and ABA closes stomata, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.

x: Auxin promotes rooting, gibberellin breaks dormancy, cytokinin drives cell division and ABA gives drought tolerance, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.

x: Auxin drives tropisms, gibberellin promotes growth, cytokinin regulates development and ABA acts as an antitranspirant, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.

x: I, II and III are correct: auxin promotes growth, apical dominance and rooting. IV is false because delaying senescence is cytokinin's job.
I, II and III are correct: gibberellin elongates cells and stems and aids germination. IV is false because closing stomata is ABA's job.
Three belong to ABA: drought tolerance, stomatal closure and growth inhibition. Delaying senescence is cytokinin.
All four are correct: auxin drives tropisms, gibberellin breaks dormancy, cytokinin drives cell division and ABA is an antitranspirant.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.

x: Ethylene (C₂H₄) is the only gaseous plant hormone, which is why one ripe fruit can ripen others nearby.
Ethylene triggers the respiratory climacteric, the burst of respiration during the ripening of fruits such as banana and mango.
Option C is incorrect: ethylene (as ethephon) stimulates latex flow in rubber trees. It promotes leaf and flower fall and senescence.
t: Recall the commercial uses of ethylene.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: fixing CO₂ into sugars is where the energy ends up; the conversion itself happens when chlorophyll captures light.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a related step.

x: I and II are correct: photosynthesis occurs in green parts, in chloroplasts. III is false because the stroma hosts the dark reaction; the light reaction is in the thylakoids.
I and II are correct: oxygen is a by-product, and CO₂ is fixed into organic compounds. III is false because of "only"; glucose is stored as starch or sucrose.
t: Check each statement for the word "only".

x: At plant level photosynthesis is in green parts, the main organ is the leaf, the tissue is mesophyll and the organelle is the chloroplast, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
The light reaction is on thylakoid membranes, the dark reaction in the stroma, chlorophyll sits in the grana and is located in chloroplasts, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall where each stage of photosynthesis happens.

x: Chlorophyll is the main pigment, it absorbs light, mainly red and blue, and reflects green, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
All four are ethylene effects: it ripens fruit, forms root hairs, inhibits stem and root elongation and stimulates latex flow.
All four are correct: glucose is the main product, stored as starch or sucrose, oxygen is a by-product and light becomes chemical energy.
Red light is the most effective for photosynthesis, absorbed strongly by chlorophyll. Green is mostly reflected.
t: Recall the action spectrum of photosynthesis.

x: Chlorophyll is located in the chloroplasts, in their thylakoid membranes. Mitochondria carry out respiration.
Chlorophyll is green because it absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
Chlorophyll has magnesium at its centre, haemoglobin iron and vitamin B₁₂ cobalt, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Recall the central metal of each molecule.

x: Both are true and R explains A: chlorophyll captures light energy, so photosynthesis cannot happen without it.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Cellular respiration happens mainly in mitochondria, glycolysis in the cytoplasm, anaerobic respiration as fermentation in the cytoplasm and aerobic respiration in mitochondria, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall where each stage of respiration happens.

x: I and II are correct: stomata are in the leaf epidermis, each a pore with guard cells. III is false because mitochondria are organelles, not where stomata are.
All four are stomatal functions: gas exchange, letting in CO₂, letting out O₂ and transpiration.
Both are true and R explains A: when guard cells swell with water the pore opens, and when they go limp it closes.
t: Check whether R is the mechanism of A.

x: I, II and III are correct: stomata carry out transpiration, potassium ions drive guard-cell swelling, and ABA closes stomata in drought. IV is false because stomata have guard cells.
t: Recall the mechanism of stomatal opening.

x: Mg is the symbol for magnesium, the central atom of chlorophyll. Fe is iron, Co cobalt and Cl chlorine.
Option C is incorrect: most transpiration happens through stomata in leaves; roots absorb water. Transpiration is loss of water vapour.
Both are true and R explains A: water evaporating from leaves pulls water up the xylem, which is the transpiration pull.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Transpiration cools leaves as water evaporates and takes heat with it, preventing overheating.
Transpiration drives upward water transport and carries minerals from root to shoot. It does not form stomata or move minerals downward.
Both are true and R explains A: ABA closes stomata, which cuts water loss.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Xerophytes such as cacti have thick cuticles, sunken stomata and reduced leaves, all of which reduce transpiration in dry places.
I and II are correct: nitrogen drives growth and is part of proteins, chlorophyll and nucleic acids. III is false because nitrogen is a macronutrient.
Phosphorus is part of ATP and nucleic acids and promotes root development. The "only" options are too narrow.
Both are true: potassium regulates stomatal opening, and calcium builds cell walls and activates enzymes.
t: Recall the role of K and Ca.

x: Sulphur is part of amino acids such as cysteine and methionine and is needed for chloroplasts and nitrogen fixation.
Iron is needed for chlorophyll synthesis and electron transport, and boron for meristem growth and nodule formation, giving a-ii, b-i.
t: Recall the role of each micronutrient.

x: Zinc supports enzymes and growth (auxin synthesis), and copper supports enzymes, giving a-ii, b-i.
t: Recall the role of each micronutrient.

x: Manganese supports photosynthesis and enzymes, and molybdenum supports nitrogen metabolism (nitrogenase), giving a-ii, b-i.
t: Recall the role of each micronutrient.

x: Both are true: chlorine and nickel are both micronutrients, needed only in tiny amounts.
Three are macronutrients: nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Iron is a micronutrient.
Three are micronutrients: iron, boron and zinc. Magnesium is a macronutrient.
Excessive transpiration causes water loss and can lead to wilting. Nodules, roots and nitrogen metabolism are unrelated.
t: Recall the effect of excessive transpiration.
